legacy_d0c4f1187c93fcba4329.content_excerpt: tim cook is departing from his long-held role as apple s ceo and a wave of top executives are heading for the exits as he does. on monday, bloomberg reported that phil schiller, long the head of apple s app store, stepped down from his position in recent days. schiller has been with the company since 1987, with only a four-year break during that time. he took over the app store in 2015. however, schiller won t be leaving the company entirely. he will be staying on as an apple fellow, a role reserved for people who have made outstanding technical or leadership contributions to the company. in that role, he will be working on unspecified projects, although bloomberg notes that insiders at the company believe that schiller s fellow role is a big step toward the executive ultimately retiring. schiller shepherded the company through a lawsuit involving epic games over the app store s in-app fee system. epic filed an antitrust lawsuit in 2020, claiming that apple had created an illegal monopoly. the monopoly claims were ultimately dismissed, and the judge in the case largely ruled in apple s favor. however, the company was still ordered to ensure that app developers could link to external payment options. the legal fight is still ongoing. as schiller steps down, apple plans to delegate day-to-day operations of the app store to carson oliver, who has been at apple for over 14 years and has worked in the app store division for the entirety of that time. the app store is also being transitioned from the marketing department to the services division, which is headed by eddy cue, bloo

legacy_956aa7e3be6e395258ef.headline: Instagram Rebrands “AI Creator” Label to “AI‑Generated Profile” and Limits Undisclosed AI Accounts
legacy_956aa7e3be6e395258ef.content_excerpt: instagram announced monday that it s changing how it labels ai-generated profiles and will start limiting the reach of accounts that feature ai-generated people without saying so. the platform says it s renaming its existing ai creator label to ai-generated profile, which instagram says should make the disclosure easier to understand. the new label is meant to tell users that the person featured on a profile was generated or substantially created with ai. under the new policy, creators who don t properly label an ai-generated profile could see their reach reduced. creators who use the new label, on the other hand, won t be penalized simply for having an ai-generated person as their profile subject. the label also isn t meant for every use of ai. instagram says people who use ai to edit photos, polish captions, create graphics, or make other creative tweaks don t need to use the ai-generated profile label. instagram says the change comes partly in response to users who have stumbled across profiles that looked like they belonged to real people, only to find out later that the person was completely ai-generated. as generative ai becomes a bigger part of how people create, we ve heard that people don t like seeing a profile that seems human, only to find out later that the person featured is ai-generated, instagram wrote. they want to know when a profile features an ai-generated person. the timing is notable. frustration over ai-generated content has been growing as ai influencers become more common across social media platforms. for instance, earlier this year, the gay dating

legacy_1d0565f9ab1ef3155f33.headline: Apple Declares 2018 MacBook Air and Two MacBook Pros Obsolete
legacy_1d0565f9ab1ef3155f33.content_excerpt: apple today added three macs to its list of obsolete products. the 2018 retina macbook air, the 13-inch 2018 macbook pro with four thunderbolt 3 ports, and the 13-inch 2017 macbook pro with two thunderbolt 3 ports are now considered obsolete. the three products were previously part of the vintage list, but have been moved. apple adds a product to the vintage list when it s been five years since it was last distributed for sale, and it becomes obsolete at the seven-year mark. vintage products can still be repaired at apple retail locations and by apple authorized service providers if apple has the parts available. devices that are obsolete are generally not eligible for repair, and apple stops making repair components. apple has a battery-only repair policy for mac laptops for up to 10 years after the mac was last distributed for sale, so 2017/2018 macbook pro and 2018 macbook air owners may still be able to get battery replacements. the 2018 macbook air was the first in the air line with touch id and a retina display. prior macbook air models had a non-retina display with much lower resolution and less vibrant colors. 2018 was also a redesign year for the macbook air, with apple introducing smaller bezels and a thinner, lighter chassis. apple s 2017 macbook pro used intel s kaby lake processors, and it was a minor processor update with few other changes. the 2018 refresh added true tone display support for the first time and a third-generation keyboard with butterfly keys.

pub_ed2f1ec68fd89af012fb.content_excerpt: - the eu just added chatgpt to its list of very large online search engines, alongside google - reddit and roblox have also been designated as very large online platforms - they ll need to adhere to greater requirements by january 2027 the european union has designated chatgpt as a very large online search engine vlose and reddit and roblox as very large online platforms vlop , putting them in the same enhanced regulatory tier as the likes of google, facebook, tiktok and amazon. the three companies triggered the switch when they amassed around 45 million monthly average users within the eu, which correlates to 10% of the bloc s rough population. importantly, the european commission effectively ended up treating chatgpt s web search functionality as part of the search market, rather than seeing the platform as a genai platform. eu adds three more platforms to its very large list chatgpt had reported around 120 million monthly users in the european union alone in september 2025, putting it way above the 45 million threshold. by march 2026 it had surpassed 159 million monthly eu users. reddit and roblox count 57 million and 48 million respectively, sitting them much closer to the threshold. as for the impacts, the vlose/vlop rules extend much further than the standard dsa requirements the three companies are already subjected to, spanning the dissemination of illegal content, the negative effects on minors, users physical and mental well-being, fundamental rights, electoral processes and public security. they ll also be subjected to greater transparency and reporting requireme

legacy_6bc0c77935aea079719a.content_excerpt: your security program was built for attackers who do. when openai published its account of the models that broke out of an evaluation environment and spent days inside hugging face s production infrastructure, i called it a terminator moment for cybersecurity. i stand by the statement, but something else about this should give us pause. nine days later, anthropic disclosed incidents of its own. in early august, meta confirmed another. days after that, a fourth lab s model, moonshot s kimi k3, was slipping its testing sandbox. four labs. less than three weeks. four models that went somewhere nobody intended. these stories have largely been treated as ai safety stories. they are. but for a ciso, they are also third-party risk stories and that may be the more immediate lesson. the uncomfortable truth is that the openai-hugging face incident was, at its core, a third-party risk story: a vulnerable third-party component as the escape route, a vendor as the victim, and a systemic node thousands of companies depend on as the blast radius. here s the number i would bring to your next security planning meeting. of the roughly 17,600 attacker actions hugging face recovered from its logs, most of them failed. the agent tested paths that went nowhere. it got blocked by url allowlists and pivoted. it hit iam policies that denied every mutating call. it tried to reach a production database twice and timed out both times. it probed, failed and moved on. thousands of times. it didn t get frustrated. it didn t get tired. and failure cost it almost nothing. four models broke out of testing e

legacy_c59b651913de610fa800.headline: EU Designates ChatGPT, Reddit, Roblox as Very Large Platforms
legacy_c59b651913de610fa800.content_excerpt: - the eu just added chatgpt to its list of very large online search engines, alongside google - reddit and roblox have also been designated as very large online platforms - they ll need to adhere to greater requirements by january 2027 the european union has designated chatgpt as a very large online search engine vlose and reddit and roblox as very large online platforms vlop , putting them in the same enhanced regulatory tier as the likes of google, facebook, tiktok and amazon. the three companies triggered the switch when they amassed around 45 million monthly average users within the eu, which correlates to 10% of the bloc s rough population. importantly, the european commission effectively ended up treating chatgpt s web search functionality as part of the search market, rather than seeing the platform as a genai platform. eu adds three more platforms to its very large list chatgpt had reported around 120 million monthly users in the european union alone in september 2025, putting it way above the 45 million threshold. by march 2026 it had surpassed 159 million monthly eu users. reddit and roblox count 57 million and 48 million respectively, sitting them much closer to the threshold. as for the impacts, the vlose/vlop rules extend much further than the standard dsa requirements the three companies are already subjected to, spanning the dissemination of illegal content, the negative effects on minors, users physical and mental well-being, fundamental rights, electoral processes and public security. they ll also be subjected to greater transparency and reporting requireme

legacy_aaae56134e8d48abc31e.headline: John Ternus Takes Helm as Apple’s New CEO Amid AI‑Driven Challenges

legacy_2b2e31179594403f9c41.headline: Renesas Joins Autoware Foundation to Deploy Open‑Source AI on R‑Car Platforms
legacy_2b2e31179594403f9c41.content_excerpt: the autoware foundation said on september 1, 2026, that renesas electronics has joined the organization as a member of its highest membership tier, in a collaboration aimed at bringing the foundation s open-source end-to-end ai software to renesas r-car system-on-chip platforms for advanced driver assistance and autonomous driving. according to the announcement, the partnership is intended to deliver pre-integrated, scalable systems for automotive original equipment manufacturers and tier-1 suppliers. the stated goal spans entry-level l2 driver assistance, scaling up to l2 hands-free autopilot and fully driverless l4 robotaxis. what the partnership delivers the collaboration introduces autoware s open-source end-to-end ai stack as a new ai driving software option for customers using renesas r-car soc and rox software platforms. under the arrangement, oems and tier-1 suppliers would be able to retrain, tune, and customize the open-source ai stack for specific vehicles and use cases, with deployment on renesas r-car socs. the foundation said the model gives automakers and suppliers an alternative to two existing paths: building an entire ai stack in-house, or purchasing a ready-made solution from a traditional commercial supplier. by building on an open-source technology substrate instead, the organizations said customers get a lower-cost and flexible option that can be internalized and customized. autoware s software is supplied under the apache 2.0 license, which the foundation said enables full commercialization without restrictions. statements from both organizations chri

pub_846d48939aaee99c4fa4.headline: Apple appoints hardware chief John Ternus as new CEO
pub_846d48939aaee99c4fa4.content_excerpt: the multitrillion-dollar home of the iphone, mac, and so many other tech gadgets has a new leaader, as tim cook has been replaced as ceo as of september 1st by former hardware boss john ternus. how will we look back on cook s legacy, and what will apple look like under the leadership of ternus and new chief hardware officer johny srouji with the next iphone event scheduled for september 9th, we ll probably find out soon. here s everything we think we know so far about the john ternus era at apple. - as much as any apple product released during his time as ceo, tim cook s tenure will be remembered for its ruthlessly efficient tight-rope walk between an autocrat in china and a would-be autocrat in the us. during his 15 years as ceo, cook steered apple through relations with both chinese president xi jinping and us president donald trump, including escalating conflicts between the two. as apple s enmeshment in china raised serious questions about reports of forced labor and censorship, cook managed to appease xi while maneuvering around political blowback in the us. and when trump launched a trade war against china, cook managed to soften the blow through his white house diplomacy. cook s ability to thread the needle between two superpowers helped expand apple into a multi-trillion-dollar company, while downplaying concerns about civil rights, working conditions, and other serious issues. read article - executive summary, day one inbox 5:05am to: ternus, john jternus apple.com reply-to: ceo-transition-team apple.com welcome to your first day as ceo hopefully you re finding you

pub_586dba2a3e71adf80648.headline: John Ternus Takes Helm as Apple’s New Chief Executive Officer
pub_586dba2a3e71adf80648.content_excerpt: apple s former hardware engineering chief john ternus officially became ceo of the company today, with the change now reflected on apple s leadership page. ternus joined apple in 2001, became a vice president of hardware engineering in 2013, and became senior vice president of hardware engineering in 2021. he is 51, so he could serve as ceo for 10 to 15 years before reaching typical retirement age. tim cook is now executive chairman of apple s board of directors, after a 15-year run as ceo. in this role, apple said cook will assist with certain aspects of the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world. during his final day as ceo on monday, cook stopped by the apple park visitor center in cupertino, california to meet some of apple s retail employees from various stores, with photos and a video of the visit available on instagram. in case you missed it, cook shared a letter to the apple community in april.

pub_a2d2d741a923f3edd74c.headline: Microsoft 365 outage persists into day two as services gradually recover
pub_a2d2d741a923f3edd74c.content_excerpt: microsoft s efforts to fix what is now a multi-day outage affecting customers access to outlook email and other microsoft 365 services are entering day two. the company made significant progress in addressing the problem on monday, after an issue impacting its exchange online service led to email delays and failures, authentication issues, and other problems for some outlook users. but as of tuesday, the issues still are not fully resolved. instead, microsoft s latest update shared on x says its mitigation actions are continuing to progress, which isn t exactly the same as saying all is well. while outlook received most of the attention, microsoft s status page for microsoft 365 business or enterprise indicates that other services were ultimately affected as well, including sharepoint, copilot, teams, purview, defender xdr, the microsoft 365 admin center, and universal print. the page attributed these to an issue with a core authentication configuration used by multiple microsoft 365 services. overnight, the company shared on x the steps that it was taking to resolve what its investigation found was a misconfiguration issue impacting its service. microsoft said the problem was preventing authentication components from deploying as expected to a portion of infrastructure. microsoft had first reviewed the recent changes that could have led to this problem, then it tested and implemented various mitigations to try to provide relief to end users. over time, as these mitigations rolled out, microsoft said outlook users should see gradual recovery to their mail flow. by 10 p.m. e

pub_96db8091cce8c60d5b7e.headline: OpenAI’s Astra Model Near Release, Claims Perfect ExploitBench Score
pub_96db8091cce8c60d5b7e.content_excerpt: openai shared new details on its forthcoming astra model, which the company said is the first large language model to meet its critical cybersecurity threshold, in preparation for its imminent release. we plan to make astra available soon, openai s blog post reads, but access to its most advanced cybersecurity capabilities will be more limited. the frontier lab determined that astra is capable of finding unknown security flaws in computer systems, and exploiting them without a person s guidance. that s similar to the concerns anthropic raised about its mythos model earlier this year, and openai is taking comparable precautions as it prepares to roll out the astra. without any third-party confirmation, it is difficult to evaluate openai s claims about safety or preparedness. the company said it would preview the model with a group of testers but did not say who they were or how they would be chosen. it s not clear if openai is working with the u.s. government to evaluate the model ahead of release. openai noted that astra scored a perfect score on exploitbench, an evaluation of an llm s ability to hack into known system vulnerabilities. in a modified version of the test developed by openai engineers, the model discovered and exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities, the company said. to ensure that its models are neither exploited by bad actors nor capable of bad behavior itself, openai said it had already begun improving the model s harness to detect abuses and prevent jailbreaks. for astra, however, the company invested in unspecified new techniques designed to make the mode

pub_fdbcbcd9313e4fe953a9.headline: Anthropic Unveils Claude Fable 5.1 After Securing $35B Lambda Cloud Deal
pub_fdbcbcd9313e4fe953a9.content_excerpt: anthropic launches claude fable 5.1 after inking $35b cloud deal with lambda anthropic pbc today debuted claude fable 5.1 and claude mythos 5.1, its most capable large language models to date. the launch comes a day after the company inked a $35 billion infrastructure deal with cloud startup lambda inc. a week earlier, anthropic signed an even larger hardware contract with nscale global holdings ltd. record-setting benchmark results fable 5.1 and mythos 5.1 are effectively the same model. the main difference is that the fable 5.1 can t be used for sensitive cybersecurity and biology tasks. mythos 5.1, which doesn t block such use cases, will be accessible to only a limited number of trusted organizations. anthropic says that fable 5.1 has set records across several ai benchmarks. it completed terminal-bench-science 0.1, a test that measures llms ability to complete research tasks, with a score of 52.6%. that s more than double what the previous-generation fable 5 model achieved. fable 5.1 also scored 13.% higher on the terminal-bench 4.0 coding benchmark and aced several non-technical task collections. another feature that sets the model apart from its predecessor is that it has more relaxed guardrails. as a result, researchers can use it to discover software vulnerabilities. however, support for more advanced tasks such as finding exploit paths is only available in mythos 5.1. anthropic says the latter llm possesses the strongest cyber capabilities of any model we ve released. mythos 5.1 is accessible through two specialized access programs for cybersecurity researchers an

pub_c9329d93e35e570d6818.headline: OpenAI Pauses Astra Development After Hugging Face Hack Highlights Safety Gaps
pub_c9329d93e35e570d6818.content_excerpt: after an unreleased openai model wreaked enough havoc to make international headlines, openai delayed the development of a different unreleased model suite, astra, in order to shore up its safety work, the company wrote tuesday in a blog post. openai delayed its new model s development after the hugging face hack the company is doing some ai safety damage control ahead of astra s release. in july, an unreleased openai model broke out of its restricted environment, finagled its way into internet access, made it possible for ai agents to secretly conspire under the company s nose using a secret message board, and hacked into the network of ai lab hugging face. the attack sparked weeks of discussion and controversy inside and outside the ai industry, and ai leaders treated it as a warning shot for the tech s growing capabilities and the inadequacy of its safeguards. openai said as much in its blog post, writing that although astra wasn t involved in the hugging face attack, the company had chosen to delay parts of astra s development and release while we strengthened and tested protections against cyber misuse and unauthorized model actions. openai also said that astra was the first model it had ever designated as meeting its ccritical cybersecurity capability threshold, meaning that it s able to find and exploit security vulnerabilities in many well-protected systems without human guidance. that means it requires stronger safeguards during development and before release, openai wrote. openai said that to prepare for astra s release which the company has not yet provided a tim

pub_ae10caa5d64c3b1cf9ac.headline: Samsung randomly deactivates Galaxy accounts citing security reasons
pub_ae10caa5d64c3b1cf9ac.content_excerpt: a bizarre issue has left many samsung galaxy owners locked out of their samsung accounts which were deactivated for security reasons. over the past 24 hours or so, a number of samsung galaxy users have taken to the web with reports of being locked out of their samsung accounts. a message appears saying that the account is deactivated. can t sign in. account deactivated for security reasons. dozens of users have reported the issue across reddit threads and samsung s community forums. samsung hasn t directly provided an explanation for the issue. this can have a pretty big impact on using a galaxy device, especially if a user is invested in samsung s software ecosystem including apps like smartthings, wallet, and find. some users appear to have had success getting back into their account with the help of support, but it s very hit or miss. while there s no clear problem at play here, it does appear that alias email addresses may play a role adding or . to an address. one support representative apparently mentioned this and a number of those affected mentioned that they do indeed use an alias of their email address for their samsung account. but not everyone affected uses an alias, so this is likely not the sole cause. samsung has yet to confirm the issue or comment on a fix beyond generic troubleshooting. we ve reached out to samsung for more information and will update this article when we hear back. if you re running into this problem, let us know in the comments below. thanks evan more on samsung: - samsung s galaxy buds are getting an fda-approved hearing aid feature - ga

pub_e3a0d530a43b2dc2ebde.headline: World Labs Unveils Atlas, Breakthrough Multimodal World Model for Spatial Intelligence
pub_e3a0d530a43b2dc2ebde.content_excerpt: fei-fei li s world labs debuts atlas, a world model showcase for advanced spatial intelligence world labs inc., the high-profile and well-funded artificial intelligence startup co-founded by the renowned computer vision pioneer fei-fei li, has just dropped atlas, which promises to be a game-changer in the world of world models. in a blog post, world labs explained that atlas is a breakthrough multimodal world model that aims to bridge the gap between simulated environments and physical reasoning. the company said atlas is an omni model, which excels in creating expansive and highly-detailed simulated 3d environments from a single image input, with precise camera control, enabling them to be viewed from any angle. the release of atlas appears to mark the fulfillment of li s overarching theory of spatial intelligence, which is the idea that if ai is to really understand and replicate the physical world, it must be able to reason natively about everything that happens within them including the 3d objects and people, the environments, how these elements interact and the spatial consequences of those interactions. introducing atlas: the world s first multimodal world model that generates image and video frames with pixel-perfect camera control and reconstructs them in 3d. model the world, move the camera, and simulate space time. pic.twitter.com/o0qegubi19 world labs theworldlabs september 1, 2026 li, who previously served as the director of stanford university s ai lab and co-founded the stanford institute for human-centered ai, launched world labs in february 2024. at the time

pub_c868ac88416b21475c93.headline: X Users Flooded with Password Reset Emails After X Money Launch

pub_168e374e5c099dda8e5c.headline: Anthropic Unveils Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with New Safeguards

pub_0531b4c6f66b061051c6.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with Tiered Safeguards
pub_0531b4c6f66b061051c6.content_excerpt: anthropic announced claude fable 5.1 and claude mythos 5.1 on september 1, 2026. the two releases are configurations of the same underlying model with different levels of safeguards: fable 5.1 is generally available, while mythos 5.1 is restricted to anthropic s trusted access programs, with safeguards designed to support work in cybersecurity and the life sciences. anthropic described the pair as its most advanced models for coding and knowledge work, and said their research capabilities offer an early glimpse of how ai models will contribute to scientific progress. availability and pricing fable 5.1 is available immediately on all platforms, including amazon web services, google cloud, and microsoft azure, and developers can access it on the claude api under the identifier claude-fable-5-1. anthropic cut the price of cache reads, where the model reuses context it has already processed, by 75%, to $0.25 per million tokens, wherever usage is billed by token. the company said this reduces typical workload costs by an estimated 25% relative to fable 5, with savings of up to approximately 45% for highly agentic work. base pricing is otherwise unchanged at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. benchmarks and research capabilities according to anthropic s published results, fable 5.1 scored 52.6% on terminal-bench-science 0.1 against 24.7% for fable 5 and 29.0% for opus 5, and 55.8% on terminal-bench 4.0, with mythos 5.1 reaching 60.9% on the same benchmark. the company reported 73.4% on cursorbench 3.2.0, 60.9% without tools and 65.0% with tools on hum

pub_6035534371fe17fb817f.headline: Google courts Hollywood studios with billion‑dollar AI licensing offers
pub_6035534371fe17fb817f.content_excerpt: google has reportedly been reaching out to a number of hollywood s biggest studios, hoping to strike licensing agreements that would allow it to train its ai models on copyrighted material in exchange for massive piles of cash. in theory, these deals would be a win-win: a huge financial boon to the studios that would also give google a significant advantage in its race to outpace other ai companies. but while there s little downside for google, these deals pose a distinct set of risks to each of the studios that might be thinking about going all-in on ai. getting into bed with google this way might benefit hollywood in the short term, but it could just as easily backfire and leave the public feeling burned by the entertainment industry. google needs hollywood more than the studios need ai striking deals with studios like disney could help the tech giant shift the narrative about artificial intelligence. though google has not yet been able to get disney, warner bros. discovery, or universal to agree to anything officially, the company s executives have been reaching out to multiple studio representatives with pitches focused on its ai technology, according to unnamed sources speaking to the los angeles times. google wants permission to train its ai models on the studios vast libraries of copyrighted content, and it s willing to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to get ahold of them. per the la times, google could pay a studio like disney / pixar around $40 million just for the rights to generate outputs featuring a single copyrighted character. that payout could swell we

pub_7e86b3c854a3ac64137b.headline: Meta launches Muse Voice Transcribe, a real‑time AI model that separates speakers and languages
pub_7e86b3c854a3ac64137b.content_excerpt: meta s new ai transcription model can distinguish between multiple speakers and languages in real-time it s the latest release from meta superintelligence lab msi . meta has introduced its first real-time audio model, muse voice transcribe. the model can handle dictation and transcription for more than 20 speakers and can seamlessly handle multiple languages at once, meta says. meta ceo mark zuckerberg, who recently returned to x after three years of not posting on the platform, shared an example of the model s ability to handle multiple speakers and languages at once. in the video, the transcription is able to automatically distinguish between multiple speakers and switch between languages. it s even able to pick up on code-switching and transcribe sentences that use words from multiple languages. muse voice transcribe is msl s first real-time audio perception model rolling out today. sota in streaming speech-to-text, it handles speaker diarization, and endpointing natively in a single model. pic.twitter.com/lvimdskbim mark zuckerberg finkd september 1, 2026 the model decides when to listen. it waits a little longer on hard words and commits faster on easy ones, using adaptive delay to predict each token and increase accuracy, he explained. it holds up on messy, real audio too trained across 70 languages with 25 validated at launch , handles mid-sentence code-switching, and manages hour-long sessions with 20 speakers. meta s release comes less than a week after google gemini 3.5 transcribe, its own audio model that boasts similar capabilities. but while google is baking it

pub_9c28c5c9d5a61719afc8.headline: CrowdStrike unveils Falcon Guardian to police AI agents on endpoints
pub_9c28c5c9d5a61719afc8.content_excerpt: crowdstrike launches falcon guardian to police ai agents at the endpoint crowdstrike holdings inc. today unveiled falcon guardian, software that finds the artificial intelligence agents running inside a company and shuts down the ones security teams have not approved. the launch came at the company s fal.con 2026 conference in las vegas. guardian is the expanded successor to falcon ai detection and response, which went generally available in december and picked up endpoint runtime protection and shadow ai discovery at the rsac conference in march. enforcement is what has been added this time. crowdstrike s argument is that the device is where an agent reasons, plans and runs code, which makes it the one place with a complete view of what that agent actually did. discovery comes first. the falcon sensor inventories known and shadow agents across windows and macos machines, both running and dormant, and logs who deployed each one along with its security status. guardian then ties agent behavior back to endpoint telemetry, building a chain that starts at a user s prompt and runs through the identity used, the tools called and the skills invoked, down to whatever the agent did to the system afterward. administrators can name which agents are permitted to run on a managed endpoint. anything not on the list gets blocked. detection and response work off the same telemetry. guardian flags attacks aimed at agents as well as agents misbehaving on their own, then reconstructs the execution chain and calculates blast radius while an incident is still in motion. crowdstrike pioneered ed

pub_9f5952080d997b1ea091.headline: AIR Security raises $50M to launch AI Agent Firewall

pub_ea5fd7b58c14960d52e0.headline: Anthropic launches Claude watermark verification API for regulators and media
pub_ea5fd7b58c14960d52e0.content_excerpt: anthropic opens claude ai text detection to regulators, media, fact-checkers, and others anthropic is launching its watermark verification api, letting approved organizations check whether text contains a digital watermark from claude. the eu ai act since august 2, 2025, requires new claude models to embed invisible watermarks in their text output. regulators, law enforcement, media, fact-checkers, independent researchers, educational organizations, and eu civil society groups can request access, as can enterprises that need to verify watermarking for their own compliance. anthropic plans to expand access over time. the system builds on google s synthid text method, tweaking word-selection randomness to create a statistically detectable pattern that, according to anthropic, may persist through some editing. that should make it far more reliable than traditional detectors like pangram. anthropic says the watermark contains no user data and affects neither quality nor content. critics disagree: if claude picks synonyms based on a watermark key rather than meaning, text quality suffers. trade publication artificial lawyer flags transparency risks too, since detectable ai fingerprints could become a problem where contracts ban ai use or during fee negotiations, though it predicts the watermarks are mostly harmless. ai news without the hype curated by humans subscribe to the decoder for ad-free reading, a weekly ai newsletter, our exclusive ai radar frontier report six times a year, full archive access, and access to our comment section. subscribe now

pub_419de7e2a1511a75f81d.headline: OpenAI Unveils Astra, First Model with Critical Cyber Capabilities

pub_b3bfa9d996f7d10521c3.headline: Google Pics Launches for Workspace Users and AI Pro Subscribers
pub_b3bfa9d996f7d10521c3.content_excerpt: google began rolling out google pics, its ai image creation and editing tool built on the company s nano banana model, to google ai pro and ultra subscribers and most workspace business customers on september 1, 2026. the tool works both as a standalone product and as an integration inside google docs and slides, with drive integration to follow in the coming weeks, google announced. the rollout moves pics beyond the limited trusted tester phase that began when google first unveiled the tool at its i/o developer conference on may 19, 2026. access is available at pics.new. precision editing features google describes pics as combining image generation with object-level editing controls. users can generate images from a text prompt or import existing images from a computer, google drive, or google photos, and the tool produces several alternatives for each prompt. the editing suite centers on what google calls object segmentation: users can isolate a specific element in an image and move, resize, or transform it without altering the rest of the picture. they can also attach text comments to specific areas to request targeted changes and run multiple edits at once, with the option to revert unwanted changes. in-image text editing lets users modify or translate words directly inside an image while preserving the original design and font style, according to the company. pics can also crop images for web, social media, print, or digital formats, and upscale them to 2k or 4k resolution. collaboration mirrors other workspace products: users can share a pics creation with a link, and

legacy_c2eeedc4bcf9522dc9e8.headline: OpenAI’s Astra Model Near Release, Claims Perfect ExploitBench Score

legacy_aa3bd54bc3e746f4c772.headline: Anthropic Unveils Claude Fable 5.1 After Securing $35B Lambda Cloud Deal

legacy_62dc796553975a076f61.headline: OpenAI Pauses Astra Development After Hugging Face Hack Highlights Safety Gaps

legacy_39c3a3811955216b6913.headline: Samsung randomly deactivates Galaxy accounts citing security reasons
legacy_39c3a3811955216b6913.content_excerpt: a bizarre issue has left many samsung galaxy owners locked out of their samsung accounts which were deactivated for security reasons. over the past 24 hours or so, a number of samsung galaxy users have taken to the web with reports of being locked out of their samsung accounts. a message appears saying that the account is deactivated. can t sign in. account deactivated for security reasons. dozens of users have reported the issue across reddit threads and samsung s community forums. samsung hasn t directly provided an explanation for the issue. this can have a pretty big impact on using a galaxy device, especially if a user is invested in samsung s software ecosystem including apps like smartthings, wallet, and find. some users appear to have had success getting back into their account with the help of support, but it s very hit or miss. while there s no clear problem at play here, it does appear that alias email addresses may play a role adding or . to an address. one support representative apparently mentioned this and a number of those affected mentioned that they do indeed use an alias of their email address for their samsung account. but not everyone affected uses an alias, so this is likely not the sole cause. samsung has yet to confirm the issue or comment on a fix beyond generic troubleshooting. we ve reached out to samsung for more information and will update this article when we hear back. if you re running into this problem, let us know in the comments below. thanks evan more on samsung: - samsung s galaxy buds are getting an fda-approved hearing aid feature - ga

legacy_97b395307eae4987ab72.headline: World Labs Unveils Atlas, Breakthrough Multimodal World Model for Spatial Intelligence
legacy_97b395307eae4987ab72.content_excerpt: fei-fei li s world labs debuts atlas, a world model showcase for advanced spatial intelligence world labs inc., the high-profile and well-funded artificial intelligence startup co-founded by the renowned computer vision pioneer fei-fei li, has just dropped atlas, which promises to be a game-changer in the world of world models. in a blog post, world labs explained that atlas is a breakthrough multimodal world model that aims to bridge the gap between simulated environments and physical reasoning. the company said atlas is an omni model, which excels in creating expansive and highly-detailed simulated 3d environments from a single image input, with precise camera control, enabling them to be viewed from any angle. the release of atlas appears to mark the fulfillment of li s overarching theory of spatial intelligence, which is the idea that if ai is to really understand and replicate the physical world, it must be able to reason natively about everything that happens within them including the 3d objects and people, the environments, how these elements interact and the spatial consequences of those interactions. introducing atlas: the world s first multimodal world model that generates image and video frames with pixel-perfect camera control and reconstructs them in 3d. model the world, move the camera, and simulate space time. pic.twitter.com/o0qegubi19 world labs theworldlabs september 1, 2026 li, who previously served as the director of stanford university s ai lab and co-founded the stanford institute for human-centered ai, launched world labs in february 2024. at the time

legacy_66165bfd9aef495df076.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with Tiered Safeguards
legacy_66165bfd9aef495df076.content_excerpt: anthropic announced claude fable 5.1 and claude mythos 5.1 on september 1, 2026. the two releases are configurations of the same underlying model with different levels of safeguards: fable 5.1 is generally available, while mythos 5.1 is restricted to anthropic s trusted access programs, with safeguards designed to support work in cybersecurity and the life sciences. anthropic described the pair as its most advanced models for coding and knowledge work, and said their research capabilities offer an early glimpse of how ai models will contribute to scientific progress. availability and pricing fable 5.1 is available immediately on all platforms, including amazon web services, google cloud, and microsoft azure, and developers can access it on the claude api under the identifier claude-fable-5-1. anthropic cut the price of cache reads, where the model reuses context it has already processed, by 75%, to $0.25 per million tokens, wherever usage is billed by token. the company said this reduces typical workload costs by an estimated 25% relative to fable 5, with savings of up to approximately 45% for highly agentic work. base pricing is otherwise unchanged at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. benchmarks and research capabilities according to anthropic s published results, fable 5.1 scored 52.6% on terminal-bench-science 0.1 against 24.7% for fable 5 and 29.0% for opus 5, and 55.8% on terminal-bench 4.0, with mythos 5.1 reaching 60.9% on the same benchmark. the company reported 73.4% on cursorbench 3.2.0, 60.9% without tools and 65.0% with tools on hum

legacy_a7890c79c0c862299179.headline: Google courts Hollywood studios with billion‑dollar AI licensing offers
legacy_a7890c79c0c862299179.content_excerpt: google has reportedly been reaching out to a number of hollywood s biggest studios, hoping to strike licensing agreements that would allow it to train its ai models on copyrighted material in exchange for massive piles of cash. in theory, these deals would be a win-win: a huge financial boon to the studios that would also give google a significant advantage in its race to outpace other ai companies. but while there s little downside for google, these deals pose a distinct set of risks to each of the studios that might be thinking about going all-in on ai. getting into bed with google this way might benefit hollywood in the short term, but it could just as easily backfire and leave the public feeling burned by the entertainment industry. google needs hollywood more than the studios need ai striking deals with studios like disney could help the tech giant shift the narrative about artificial intelligence. though google has not yet been able to get disney, warner bros. discovery, or universal to agree to anything officially, the company s executives have been reaching out to multiple studio representatives with pitches focused on its ai technology, according to unnamed sources speaking to the los angeles times. google wants permission to train its ai models on the studios vast libraries of copyrighted content, and it s willing to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to get ahold of them. per the la times, google could pay a studio like disney / pixar around $40 million just for the rights to generate outputs featuring a single copyrighted character. that payout could swell we

legacy_3acda2aabad79cefce06.headline: Meta launches Muse Voice Transcribe, a real‑time AI model that separates speakers and languages
legacy_3acda2aabad79cefce06.content_excerpt: meta s new ai transcription model can distinguish between multiple speakers and languages in real-time it s the latest release from meta superintelligence lab msi . meta has introduced its first real-time audio model, muse voice transcribe. the model can handle dictation and transcription for more than 20 speakers and can seamlessly handle multiple languages at once, meta says. meta ceo mark zuckerberg, who recently returned to x after three years of not posting on the platform, shared an example of the model s ability to handle multiple speakers and languages at once. in the video, the transcription is able to automatically distinguish between multiple speakers and switch between languages. it s even able to pick up on code-switching and transcribe sentences that use words from multiple languages. muse voice transcribe is msl s first real-time audio perception model rolling out today. sota in streaming speech-to-text, it handles speaker diarization, and endpointing natively in a single model. pic.twitter.com/lvimdskbim mark zuckerberg finkd september 1, 2026 the model decides when to listen. it waits a little longer on hard words and commits faster on easy ones, using adaptive delay to predict each token and increase accuracy, he explained. it holds up on messy, real audio too trained across 70 languages with 25 validated at launch , handles mid-sentence code-switching, and manages hour-long sessions with 20 speakers. meta s release comes less than a week after google gemini 3.5 transcribe, its own audio model that boasts similar capabilities. but while google is baking it

legacy_50619853f5fb11860910.content_excerpt: google began rolling out google pics, its ai image creation and editing tool built on the company s nano banana model, to google ai pro and ultra subscribers and most workspace business customers on september 1, 2026. the tool works both as a standalone product and as an integration inside google docs and slides, with drive integration to follow in the coming weeks, google announced. the rollout moves pics beyond the limited trusted tester phase that began when google first unveiled the tool at its i/o developer conference on may 19, 2026. access is available at pics.new. precision editing features google describes pics as combining image generation with object-level editing controls. users can generate images from a text prompt or import existing images from a computer, google drive, or google photos, and the tool produces several alternatives for each prompt. the editing suite centers on what google calls object segmentation: users can isolate a specific element in an image and move, resize, or transform it without altering the rest of the picture. they can also attach text comments to specific areas to request targeted changes and run multiple edits at once, with the option to revert unwanted changes. in-image text editing lets users modify or translate words directly inside an image while preserving the original design and font style, according to the company. pics can also crop images for web, social media, print, or digital formats, and upscale them to 2k or 4k resolution. collaboration mirrors other workspace products: users can share a pics creation with a link, and

pub_d907fde100c13abd8c8f.headline: Microsoft Rolls Out Windows 11 Memory‑Integrity Security, May Slow PC Gaming
pub_d907fde100c13abd8c8f.content_excerpt: microsoft is getting ready to roll out its memory integrity security feature of windows 11 to more devices next month. the kernel-level protection feature is designed to stop malicious code or drivers running on a windows 11 machine, but microsoft previously warned it can also impact pc gaming performance. microsoft is enabling a windows 11 security feature that can hurt gaming performance memory integrity could get enabled on your device next month, unless you ve already disabled it. windows quality updates will begin enabling memory integrity protection on eligible devices, says peter waxman, group program manager at microsoft. if not already enabled, these updates will also enable virtualization-based security vbs , helping make additional security capabilities available and reflecting our commitment to making windows secure by design and secure by default. while memory integrity only allows trusted kernel-mode code and drivers to run on a windows 11 system, it also impacts pc game performance on certain hardware. there s less of an impact if you have a more modern cpu, but you might notice more of a frame-rate drop in select games on older processors. microsoft won t automatically enable memory integrity again next month if you ve already previously disabled the feature. if you want to check whether memory integrity is enabled on your windows 11 pc, you can type core isolation into windows search and then open the result and toggle memory integrity on or off in the windows security app. if you decide to disable this security feature in favor of more pc gaming performanc

pub_56db5671053646a28e14.headline: Google Messages Adds Content Credentials to Flag AI‑Edited Media in Android Chats
pub_56db5671053646a28e14.content_excerpt: google messages just made it easier to spot ai-edited photos in your group chats sep 2, 2026 5:08 am et - google messages now supports content credentials, letting you check how compatible photos, videos, and audio were created or edited, including whether ai tools were involved. - it won t tell you whether something is real or fake. content credentials only show the history attached to a file, and media without credentials won t provide this information. - the feature is currently android-only. press and hold supported media, tap info, and look for how this was made to see its origin and editing history. a couple of months ago, we spotted google messages preparing a useful new trick for the age of ai: a way to tell you about where the photos, videos, and audio people send you actually came from. that feature is now available, and it could come in handy the next time something in your group chat looks too good to be true. google messages now supports content credentials, which essentially give compatible media a digital history. instead of leaving you to stare at a suspicious photo and wonder whether it was shot with a camera, heavily edited, or created with the help of ai, messages can show you some of that information directly. there is one important limitation, though. google messages can t tell you whether something is real or fake. it can only show you the history recorded with that file. so, if the file contains content credentials showing that ai tools were used to edit it, you now have a pretty useful clue before forwarding it to someone else. the feature also won t

pub_d548f2827a69f901a667.headline: Acer Launches Compact SFF RTX Spark Desktop for On‑Device Agentic AI

pub_483fb38296fd6a76ed33.headline: Acer Confirms First Googlebook Arrival Ahead of September 15 Launch Event
pub_483fb38296fd6a76ed33.content_excerpt: acer googlebook is officially coming soon, and here s a first glimpse sep 2, 2026 6:24 am et - acer has announced that its first googlebook is coming soon. - the company didn t reveal more launch details, but we re guessing it could appear at the googlebook launch event on september 15. - acer also gave us a fleeting glimpse of the machine, revealing what appears to be a conventional laptop. google will hold its googlebook launch event on september 15, and we re expecting many devices from hardware partners. now, acer has confirmed that it ll soon offer a googlebook of its own, while giving us a fleeting glimpse at the device. acer confirmed at its ifa 2026 event that its first googlebook is coming soon, without revealing more availability details. it s a safe bet that we ll learn more about acer s new computer at the september 15 launch. otherwise, the company also gave us a glimpse of its new googlebook. there isn t much to glean from the images, but it looks like a conventional laptop rather than a detachable device. we can also see a google pixel phone next to the laptop, hinting at the previously disclosed cross-device integration. previous acer googlebook leaks hint at a machine with an intel core ultra 5 chip, 16gb of ram, a 256gb ssd, and a 14-inch 120hz oled screen. we can t rule out variants with more impressive internals, either. this wasn t the only news acer had at ifa 2026, though. it also announced an epaper monitor, the crazy project dualplay mini concept handheld, new swift laptops, and new iconia android tablets.
